sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax
sections.html:
Two offices handle Crawford County property tax. One of them mails and collects bills. The other decides what each parcel is worth. A seller usually needs to call both.

Find the Tax Commissioner at 640 GA Hwy 128 in Roberta, weekdays 8:15 am to 4:45 pm, holidays excepted, or call (478) 836-3575. Bills for real and personal property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber all come from here. Appeals and name or address changes do not.

The assessors, at (478) 836-2800, take returns, exemption applications and written appeals. A house inside Roberta may also owe city tax, which is collected at Roberta City Hall.

This is west central Georgia, within the Macon metro area, with the courthouse in Knoxville and the largest town in Roberta. About 325 square miles of land hold roughly 37 people per square mile, so most parcels are rural and many include acreage. If you are selling only part of a tract, ask the assessors how a split is treated.

Estimates for July 2025 show 12,206 residents and 5,388 housing units, and 81.4 percent of homes have their owners living in them. Median home value is $164,100 and rent runs $914 a month. Few households change addresses from one year to the next.

Match your question to the right desk before you phone.

sections.h2: When is Crawford County property tax due?
sections.html:
Real estate is usually due December 20. The bills typically go out in mid-October and carry the name of whoever held title when the year began.

A county may shift that to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments, and interest does not begin until 60 days after the postmark. Check the date on your own bill before you schedule a closing.

  • Late tax accrues interest monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, reset each calendar year from the first weekly Federal Reserve posting.
  • A further 5 percent penalty lands at every 120-day mark past the due date.
  • Once a bill is placed on the General Execution Docket, FiFa charges are added.
  • Mobile homes taxed off-digest fall due May 1 and then draw a 10 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest monthly.

Lenders do not get bills from this office. Owners with escrow should check that the servicer has the figures, and anyone whose mailed copy never showed up can request a duplicate.

sections.h2: How the tax amount is set
sections.html:
Tax is 40 percent of the assessors' fair market value multiplied by the millage rate, with the parcel valued as of January 1. The county commissioners choose one rate and the school board another. The garbage fee appears on the same statement.

A rollback rate is the rate that would collect last year's revenue after values rise. Going above it means three public hearings. Its news section carries the tax digest and a five-year levy history.

Get the millage for your parcel from the Tax Commissioner. Last year's bill is an unreliable guide because both boards can change rates annually.

Appeals go in writing to the Tax Assessors, never the Tax Commissioner. You have 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed, and notices usually arrive in spring.

Filing a return during the first three months of the year lets you put your own value on record. You need not file every year. Because the appeal must be postmarked inside the window, keep a mailing receipt.

If the Board of Assessors leaves the value unchanged, ask the assessors' office what the next level of appeal is and what deadline applies. A seller who gets a spring notice shortly before listing the house should read it closely, since the value feeds that year's bill and a buyer's expectations.

Homestead is the big one. You can apply year-round, but April 1 closes the digest. To qualify you must own the house, live in it on January 1, claim Georgia as your legal residence and hold title in your own name. Service members must also name Georgia as their home state.

  • Added relief begins at 62, and the applicant must have reached that age by January 1 of the filing year.
  • Disability claims need statements of total disability from two separate sources.
  • A military service exemption is also offered through the assessors.
  • Agricultural, preferential, conservation use, historic and tax-exempt status all run through the same office.

Skipping the application counts as waiving the exemption. An heir who takes over a house should ask the assessors about filing in the new owner's name instead of assuming the old one carries over.

Four steps help a Crawford County seller avoid surprises. Phone the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure and ask about any city bill if the house is in Roberta. Check with the assessors on whether your homestead exemption is on file and whether any acreage is enrolled in a special program. Read the spring assessment notice so you know the value a buyer will see. Then put the tax split in writing in the contract.

A cash buyer can skip a lender's appraisal and move faster, but the payoff, the January 1 owner rule and the exemption change at closing all still apply. After the sale, the buyer files for their own exemption.

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff before signing anything. The office tells people mailing overdue payments to phone first, because penalties and execution charges move the total.

The statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so a seller closing in the fall is the named taxpayer for that year. Put the split in the sale contract and ask the closing agent to carry the payoff into the settlement numbers.

Mobile homes add a step. All taxes must be paid and a current decal displayed before one is moved out of the county.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Crawford County property tax?
faqs.a: In person at 640 GA Hwy 128, Suite 134, in Roberta, or by mail to P.O. Box 634 in the same town. The office takes checks, cash, money orders and credit or debit cards, and online payment is available.

faqs.q: Does Crawford County mail my tax bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. The office does not bill lenders. If you pay through escrow, make sure the servicer has the amount, and phone (478) 836-3575 for a duplicate if yours never arrived.

faqs.q: Who do I contact to change the owner name on a Crawford County parcel?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessors, at (478) 836-2800. Notices go to the last known address of the January 1 owner, and the commissioner's desk does not process these updates.

faqs.q: Can I still file for homestead in Crawford County after April 1?
faqs.a: You can still turn in the form, but it will not reach that year's digest, because April 1 is the cutoff.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Crawford County value after the deadline?
faqs.a: A late appeal risks being turned away, because it must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. Keep the notice, note that date, and mail your written appeal to the Tax Assessors well ahead of the last day.
